title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 28
paragraphs: Such was what the Phokians had done to the Thessalian foot-soldiers when besieged by them; and they had also done irreparable harm to their cavalry when it invaded their country. For in the pass near Hyampolis they had dug a great trench and laid down empty wine-jars in it; then, having brought earth and laid it on top and made it look like the rest of the ground, they waited for the Thessalians to invade. These, supposing they would make short work of the Phokians, charged in full gallop and fell upon the wine-jars; there the legs of their horses were utterly smashed.
